title: Q2 QBR - Suncrest Retail - Health Check
summary: QBR focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents in Q2, and roadmap alignment. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send detailed cost breakdown, propose batching and quantization tweaks for checkout model, schedule a technical deep-dive for private VPC migration planning.
next_steps: Maya to send Q2 token-level usage and cost breakdown (by route) - due 2026-07-20
Priya Nair to schedule cost-optimization deep-dive w/ Suncrest infra team - due 2026-07-27
Redwood to share security docs (SOC 2/ISO/SSO + KMS integration notes) - due 2026-07-19
Suncrest to confirm pilot scope for private VPC trial - due 2026-07-30

Priya Nair - Run initial quantization/batching simulation for checkout model, share expected cost delta - 2026-07-27

header: Date: 2026-07-16 | Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Liam O'Connor, Priya Rao, Evelyn Park, Jordan Miles (Suncrest)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time for the QBR. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, hi Maya.
[00:08] Priya Rao: Priya here from platform.
[00:10] Evelyn Park: Evelyn - product.
[00:12] Jordan Miles: Jordan - SRE.
[00:14] Diego Alvarez: Diego from Redwood CSM.
[00:16] Priya Nair: Priya Nair, SE.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great. Agenda 
— we'll run through usage and cost, reliability incidents in Q2, roadmap items, then next steps. We'll try to leave 10 minutes for open discussion.
[01:05] Maya Chen: To start: in Q2 overall token usage was up ~24% quarter-over-quarter, the majority coming from the checkout recommendation route and the support chat embeddings. Liam, is that in line with what you're seeing on your side?
[01:20] Liam O'Connor: Yeah that sounds right. We had the promo launch mid-May which drove more chat volume. A few bot flows started being used more heavily; we didn't expect that much spike on the embeddings.
[01:32] Evelyn Park: The marketing team rolled out conversational upsells so that explains it. We're concerned about cost — that spike felt larger than forecast.
[01:40] Priya Rao: Cost is the big ask. Our finance team flagged the monthly invoice as 18% over budget for the model usage line.
[01:48] Maya Chen: Understood. Diego, can you give the high-level cost drivers we saw on Redwood's side?
[01:55] Diego Alvarez: Sure. Roughly speaking, the delta came from three things: increased token volume (as Maya said), longer average sequence length for support chats (we saw average context grow from 340 to ~520 tokens), and a shift to gen-large model for some A/B tests during the promo window. We also saw a small percentage of failed retries that contributed to extra tokens.
[02:20] Jordan Miles: About the retries — we had two brief incidents where routing fell back to hosted and retried a few requests, that was the incident mid-May?
[02:28] Priya Nair: I have the incident notes here. On 2026-05-18 there was a transient network partition in eu-west-1 that caused routing to fall back to the global pool for about 12 minutes; some requests retried. Recovery was automatic but that created duplication.
[02:42] Maya Chen: Right, Diego will share the incident timeline. For cost optimization, we usually look at batching, prefix caching, and model quantization. Priya (SE), do you have quick wins we can propose for the checkout flow?
[02:57] Priya Nair: Yep. For checkout recommendations, the model is currently running as fp16 gen-large. We can try 8-bit quantized variant which usually is a 30-45% cost drop with <1% quality delta for structured recommendation tasks. Also we can enable smarter batching — the route has predictable short sequences so increasing batch window to 20ms and enabling dynamic padding can reduce per-token overhead.
[03:23] Evelyn Park: How risky is quantization? We need to keep conversion recommendations accurate.
[03:28] Priya Nair: There's a small risk, which is why we recommend an A/B style rollout — run batch on a slice of traffic and monitor top-K recall and conversion delta. We can provide the regression eval harness and baseline metrics.
[03:40] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. We'd need the quantized model hostable in our dedicated pool — is that supported?
[03:45] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports quantized variants; we'll include the config and perf numbers.
[03:50] Diego Alvarez: We'll also include per-route latency percentiles so you can see P50/P95/P99 differences.
[04:05] Maya Chen: Switching to reliability — Jordan flagged two SLO misses in June, can you walk through what happened?
[04:12] Jordan Miles: Sure. On 2026-06-09 we observed increased 5xx rates for the support-chat route, P95 latency spiked to ~2.1s for 20 minutes. Root cause was a degraded NVMe instance in the dedicated pool that affected a subset of shards. Failover worked but there was a delayed drain.
[04:33] Diego Alvarez: That is correct, the runtime detected the disk I/O error and removed the node from rotation but the in-flight KV cache warming caused a latency tail while new nodes warmed. We shipped a patch to improve drain behavior.
[04:46] Priya Nair: We recommended enabling automatic prefix caching and warm-start policies for the pool — those significantly lower the tail when a node gets evicted.
[04:55] Maya Chen: Great — will you share the patch and the remediation notes?
[04:58] Diego Alvarez: Yep, included in next steps.
[05:10] Maya Chen: On the roadmap side, we have upcoming features — on the console we released token-level cost breakdowns and an experimental workload-aware autoscaler last month. Diego, brief on what's available to Suncrest today?
[05:24] Diego Alvarez: Token-level breakdown is available in the Billing tab; there's an API export for per-route stats. The autoscaler is in early beta; it supports custom policies (throughput or latency SLO driven). We can give you access to the beta for your dedicated pool.
[05:38] Evelyn Park: That autoscaler could help control bursts during marketing events. What's the guardrail around cost when autoscaling? We don't want runaway spend.
[05:46] Maya Chen: You can set a max-capacity parameter and a billing alert threshold; also the autoscaler supports burst capacity caps. We'll include recommended settings for promo windows.
[05:58] Priya Rao: On Private deployment — Suncrest is still considering a VPC-private control plane pilot. We wanted to revisit timeline and constraints.
[06:07] Maya Chen: Yes. From Redwood's side, Private VPC pilot typically takes 6-8 weeks for initial onboarding depending on networking and audit windows. Key items we need: a list of compliance stakeholders, your preferred KMS, and whether you need on-prem package or VPC only.
[06:22] Liam O'Connor: Compliance wants audit logs retention 18 months and a SOC 2 bridge. Also we use AWS KMS and require customer-managed keys.
[06:31] Diego Alvarez: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS integration and can provide extended log retention as an add-on. We'll surface the exact SLA and bridge docs.
[06:40] Maya Chen: We'll share the security pack and a draft timeline.
[06:44] Priya Nair: For the private pilot, we usually run a dry-run manifest that includes a perf baseline — we'll need 48 hours of representative traffic for measurements.
[06:53] Jordan Miles: We'll coordinate offline to schedule that window.
[07:00] Maya Chen: Quick open question — any blockers from your side for the pilot?
[07:05] Liam O'Connor: Mainly internal compliance sign-off and a short procurement review, but nothing blocking from a tech perspective.
[07:12] Evelyn Park: On product side, we want to prioritize cost reduction on the checkout route; if we can get a 25-30% saving that's a win.
[07:20] Priya Nair: I think quant+batch + routing to a cheaper model variant for non-critical recs can hit that. We'll simulate and share numbers.
[07:27] Maya Chen: Next, let's quickly recap the incidents and the fixes: the eu-west transient partition (mid-May) and the NVMe degraded node (June) — we'll send the playbooks for both.
[07:38] Diego Alvarez: Action items captured: cost breakdown, quantization simulation, incident playbooks, security docs, and scheduling the private pilot window.
[07:48] Maya Chen: Anything else from Suncrest?
[07:52] Priya Rao: One ask — can Redwood share a sample billing alert policy that ties to per-route spend? We want to implement it before next promo.
[07:59] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we'll send sample alert thresholds and an alerting runbook.
[08:05] Evelyn Park: Thanks.
[08:07] Maya Chen: Alright, we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the deep-dive. Thanks everyone for the time.
[08:14] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.
[08:16] (meeting ends)
notes: Transcript includes minor ASR errors and occasional speaker label mismatches; timestamps approximate. References: shared Q2 usage spreadsheet (link sent in chat), security pack PDF (to be shared).
